svg.title: What crosses the network, and what does not
svg.desc: On the left, things that never leave the device: the photo itself (the API has no image upload endpoint at all), the precise GPS position, the Gemma 3n verifier and the inference that runs it, and the field-test log kept in localStorage. On the right, everything the server ever receives: a random device UUID, coordinates rounded to three decimals, enum-only mood and persona with interests sanitized to keywords, the verification verdict of match, confidence and a short description, elapsed and visible seconds, place ids with public OpenStreetMap coordinates, and within_radius as a boolean after the check-in position is scored and discarded. A footer states the honest limit: this is not a fully offline app, the claim is that photos and exact movements stay on the device while the server sees an approximate area.
svg.text: The privacy boundary is a property of the architecture, not a promise in a policy
Never leaves your device
There is no code path that could send these.
The photo
Drawn to a canvas, handed to the model in memory.
The API has no upload endpoint, no UploadFile, no
multipart handler. All 11 endpoints are JSON only.
Where you actually are
The browser rounds to 3 decimals before the first
request. Nothing finer than that exists to send.
The verifier itself
Gemma 3n weights sit in OPFS; MediaPipe runs them
on WebGPU. Verified in airplane mode as proof.
The field-test log
localStorage, capped at 500 rows, no network path at
all. No coordinates, no place names, no quest titles,
no wall-clock time. You export the CSV by hand.
Clearable there, and wiped by "delete my data".
Tests assert each of these, not comments.
request
quest back
HTTPS only
32 KB body cap
CORS pinned to
one origin
Rate limited
per device
Everything the server ever sees
This is the whole list, not a summary of it.
A random UUID in X-Device-Id
No email, no name, no password, no account. Hashed
to 16 hex characters before it reaches a trace.
An area, never a point
lat/lng at 3 decimals, about 110 m, re-rounded server
side and never written to any collection.
Enums and sanitized keywords
mood, persona, mode come from closed sets. Interests
are stripped to letters, digits, spaces and hyphens.
The verdict, not the evidence
{match, confidence, seen} plus elapsed_seconds and
screen_seconds. "seen" is 12 words at most.
Place ids and public OSM coordinates
Coordinates of a public park, not of a person. An
optional check-in is scored into within_radius: true
or false, and the position itself is thrown away.
DELETE /v1/profile removes all of it.
The honest version of the claim
This is not a fully offline app, and the README does not say it is. The deployed build needs the network to find places and to speak.
What is true: photos and exact movements stay on your device, and the server sees an approximate area in order to find nearby places.
